lanes.evidence: Leftmost lane at the stop bar, next to the tree-lined median. Satellite shows a left-turn arrow in it about 6 m before the stop bar, and a second left arrow further upstream. A solid white line separates it from lane 2. C1 (look-back) shows the left-turn arrow and the word ONLY in this lane on the photo's right side (the driver's left), next to the grass median. C2 (forward) shows ONLY in the left lane.

Lane right of the solid lane line. Satellite shows a straight-ahead arrow in it, with another one upstream, and a car standing at the stop bar in this lane. C1 shows a large through arrow in this lane, pointing toward the junction. A solid white line on its right separates it from the narrow curbside bicycle strip. No right-turn arrow is visible.

response.limitations: Building shadow covers most of the satellite approach, so faint markings are hard to read. The curbside strip, between a solid white line and the curb with brick sidewalk, holds no parked cars. It carries a worn symbol in C1 and is read as a bicycle lane. In the satellite, the line between lane 2 and this strip is visible upstream but not in the last ~7 m before the stop bar (shadow, maybe dashed or ending). C1, however, shows it solid well past the arrows. So it is not certain whether right-turning motor vehicles enter the strip at the stop bar, and it is not counted as a lane. The opposing carriageway beyond the median on the left is excluded. The street views date from 2020-11 and the satellite date is unknown.
